title: Patient-oriented provision of aids for bladder and bowel dysfunction in people with multiple sclerosis
summary:
Multiple sclerosis (MS) is the most common chronic inflammatory degenerative disease of the central nervous system in young adults, with up to 15,000 new cases diagnosed each year. MS is also known as the disease with 1,000 faces because the symptoms and manifestations are diverse and individual. Nevertheless, MS has one thing in common: after 15 years, many people with the disease develop bladder and bowel dysfunction (including urinary and fecal incontinence). Incontinence problems are often diagnosed too late due to shame, which can lead to delayed treatment and restrictions in everyday social life.
The MS-Vita project aims to significantly improve the quality of life of those affected by showing ways of early diagnosis with individually adapted incontinence management and appropriate provision of aids. To this end, affected people, their relatives and members of the various healthcare professions involved, such as nurses, physiotherapists and doctors, are surveyed. Furthermore, anonymous routine data, for example from health insurance companies, will be evaluated in order to improve the treatment of people with MS. In addition, the research findings will be used to derive recommendations for the needs-based provision of aids for bladder and bowel emptying disorders.
conditions: Demyelinating diseases of the central nervous system

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
# Ability to communicate sufficiently in German
# Nursing degree 0-5
# Affiliation to the mentioned health professions with corresponding specialization
# Professional experience of at least 1 year
Exclusion criteria:
# under 18 years of age
# not able to communicate sufficiently in German
# Care level 0 or 3 and higher
# Belonging to professional groups not in focus
# lack of professional experience
